A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, 12 figures, Table 1, and appendices A–G. The reordered appendices can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on Boolean latent recovery, polynomial extrapolation, and prediction of parabolic and collision motion in Section 5 and Appendices C and G.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices D and G.

M1.justification: The mixed-activation MLP and its application within transformers are unchanged. Both versions retain the same activation proportions, training objectives, and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Boolean latent-variable tasks, degree-1–3 polynomial extrapolation, and parabolic and elastic-collision motion under the same distribution shifts. Moving numerical experiments from Appendix C to D adds no coverage.

E2.justification: ReLU MLPs remain the polynomial comparators, and the standard transformer remains the physical-motion comparator. The Boolean experiments retain their comparisons with and without an oracle representation.

E3.justification: Appendix F retains the same data ranges, sample counts, model configurations, training budgets, and MSE evaluation. Motion prediction still observes three of 32 frames and autoregressively predicts the remaining 29.

E4.justification: Figures 3–5 retain the low-degree-bias, task-count, and oracle-representation analyses. The supplementary polynomial examples and collision case study in Appendix G are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 2(c) still averages physical-motion results over five runs, and polynomial violin plots retain 50 sampled polynomials. No seed disclosures, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and graphics are unchanged. Figure 2(c) retains Transformer/Ours MSEs of 0.16/0.07 for parabolic motion and 0.29/0.13 for collision; Figure 12 retains 0.0039 for Ours and 0.5090 for Transformer.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.12(ii) expands from an existence claim about problematic incompatible bases to asserting that every incompatible basis prevents degree-1 recovery. It also explicitly quantifies the construction over every k in [d]. Appendix E.8 adds an equivalence argument supporting this substantially stronger statement.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the principal claims about multi-task learning, low-degree bias, latent recovery, architecture sensitivity, and empirical advantages. The contribution list more explicitly names the already-present Boolean formulation.

C2.justification: The revised architecture result states a stricter failure boundary by explicitly ruling out degree-1 recovery whenever the basis is incompatible. The empirical interpretations, degree-1-task sampling caveat, and Section 6 limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains the same data-generation instructions, activation proportions, hyperparameters, optimizers, PyTorch implementation information, and V100/A100 hardware disclosure. No code or data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained, including comparisons with latent-variable identification research, implicit-bias analyses, and Xu et al. (2021). Updated appendix references reflect relocation.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited prose and notation edits and adds the missing Section 5.2 heading. Boolean preliminaries move from D to B, complexity discussion from B to C, and numerical experiments from C to D; the main narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 and Figures 3–5 move from pages 16–17 to pages 17–18 following appendix reordering. There are minor caption edits and text reflow, but no figures or tables are added, removed, or redrawn.

improvement.justification: Small navigation and notation improvements are outweighed by the new universal claim in Theorem 4.12(ii). Under Equation (11), the invertible map U(1)=1+z1 that fixes all other parity functions is incompatible, yet changes only constant-task costs and leaves optimal representations unchanged. This contradicts the added universal failure claim and introduces a localized theoretical error; the other main results and experiments are retained.
